title: Service improvement and growth
audience: Any owner or manager who wants to grow the business by improving services and winning repeat and additional work in any service business.
learningOutcomes: Identify the service improvements that increase repeat work without reducing safety or quality.
Describe how to offer additional services that the team can deliver safely and profitably.
Measure the effect of a change before deciding whether to keep it.

instruction.heading: Grow by doing the current job better
instruction.body: The most reliable growth in a service business comes from repeat customers who are satisfied with the scope, the timing, the communication and the result. Use the job records and the customer feedback to find the points where the service fails or delights. A missed item that causes a complaint, a late arrival that is not communicated, or a product that leaves a residue are all improvements. Choose one improvement at a time, make it, and check whether it reduced the complaint or increased repeat work.

instruction.heading: Add services the team can deliver safely
instruction.body: Additional services can increase revenue, but only when they match the team's skills, equipment and licences. Before offering a new service, check the scope, the hazards, the licence requirement and the price, using the service offer and pricing lessons. A recommended add-on, such as an oven clean for a regular kitchen client, should be defined with its scope, time and price, and offered only where it can be done safely. List it on the written quote as a separate option, so the customer can choose it. Do not offer a restricted or licensed service that the business does not hold the licence for. Licence and training rules differ by state or territory and by type of work, so check the rule where you operate.

instruction.heading: Measure before you keep a change
instruction.body: Decide in advance what result a change should produce, such as fewer complaints, more repeat bookings, or less time per job. Record the measure before and after the change, and review it after a fixed period. A change that does not produce the result is reviewed or reversed. Do not claim growth from a single job or from a feeling. Keep the record so that the decision can be explained to the team and the customer.

procedure: Review the job records and customer feedback for repeated failures and successes.
Choose one improvement and record the measure it should improve.
Check the scope, hazards, licence and price of any new add-on service before offering it.
Offer the add-on only where the team can deliver it safely and profitably.
Record the measure before the change and review it after a fixed period.
Keep the change if it works, and review or reverse it if it does not.

workedExamples.situation: Three customers in one month complain that the kitchen floor is still sticky after the clean. The team wants to offer a new floor-sealing service to fix the problem.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the business do first?
workedExamples.reasoning: Look for the cause before offering a new service. The sticky floor may be caused by product over-dosing or insufficient rinsing. Check the dosing and the rinse step, and record the measure: number of sticky-floor complaints per month. Review after a month. Only consider the new service after the cause is confirmed and the team can deliver it safely.

equipmentAndPpe: Job records and customer feedback log

commonErrors.error: Adding a service to fix a problem whose cause has not been found.
commonErrors.prevention: Find the cause in the job records before offering a new service.

commonErrors.error: Claiming growth from a single job or an impression.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure before and after the change over a fixed period.

commonErrors.error: Offering a licensed or restricted service the team cannot deliver.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the scope, licence and hazards before offering any add-on.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: An add-on service must meet the same hazard assessment, licence and training requirements as the main service, where those rules apply. Offering the add-on does not change those requirements. The rules depend on the state or territory and on the work, so check them with the relevant regulator before the add-on is offered.

qualityStandard: Each improvement is linked to a recorded measure and a review date.
No add-on is offered until its scope, hazards, licence and price are confirmed.
Changes that do not produce the measured result are reviewed or reversed.
documentationEvidence: Improvement log with the measure, the change, the review date and the outcome.
Add-on service definition with scope, hazards, licence and price.
summary: Grow by fixing the causes of complaints and delivering consistently.
Add only services the team can deliver safely, with the right licence.
Measure before and after each change, and keep only what works.

knowledgeChecks.question: Several customers complain about the same issue. What should you do first?
options: Find the cause in the job records before changing the service.
Add a new service straight away for every customer on the list.
Close the complaints, since a few cases are not a pattern.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before offering an add-on service, what must be confirmed?
options: Only that customers really want it and will pay
Its scope, hazards, licence requirement and price.
That a competitor offers it and that the price is lower.

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say a change should be reviewed?
options: After a fixed period, with measures recorded before and after the change
